12.text: In the sieve elements, which one of the following is the most likely function of P-proteins ?
options: Deposition of callose on sieve plates
12.sol: Sieve elements are a component of phloem tissue and are responsible for conduction of food in plants. A sieve tube element has peripheral layer of cytoplasm without any nucleus. The central part is occupied by a network of canals which contain fibrils of $p$-protein. The protein is vibratite and is believed to actively participate in the transport of nutrients. One general property of its ability to form a gel and it functions as a puncture repair substance forming a plug at any site of damage in sieve element, thus preventing loss of food materials being translocated by the phloem. Thus it is believed to have sealing function on wounding.

1963.subject: Zoology
1963.text:
Assertion : Blood coagulate in uninjured blood vessels.
Reason : Uninjured blood vessels release an anticoagulant heparin.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1963.sol: When a blood vessel gets injured, blood platelets get clumped at the injured spot and release certain chemicals called platelet factors, which promote blood coagulation. Injured tissues or platelets also release coagulation promoting substances called thromboplastins which help in the formation of an enzyme prothrombinase. This enzyme activates inactive protein prothrombin to active thrombin which further promotes the coagulation process. Blood normally contains an anticoagulant heparin which is released from mast cell granules that prevents the activation of prothrombin in uninjured blood vessels. Blood also contains antithrombin which inhibits any thrombin formed accidentally. Moreover, uninjured tissues do not release thromboplastins, hence blood does not coagulate in uninjured blood vessels.

3891.text: Order of acidity of benzoic acid (I), 4-methoxybenzoic acid (II), acetic acid (III) and 4-nitrobenzoic acid (IV) is
3891.sol:
An electron-donating group decreases the strength of acids, while electron withdrawing group increases the strength of acids. A methoxy group is clectron donating group, 4-methoxy benzoic acid is a weaker acid than benzoic acid. Nitro group is electron withdrawing group and will increase the strength of acids. Thus, correct order is
4-nitrobenzoic acid (IV) > benzoic acid (I) > 4-methoxy benzoic acid (II) > acetic acid (III)

6199.text: Find the coordinates of a point on the curve $y=x^2-3 x+2$, at which the tangent drawn to this curve is perpendicular to the line $y=x$.
6199.sol:
Given curve, $y=x^2-3 x+2$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x,
\frac{d y}{d x}=2 x-3$
Which represents the slope of tangent drawn to the curve.
$m_1=2 x-3$...(i)
Given line, $\quad y=x$...(ii)
On comparing with $y=m x+c$
Slope of line (ii), $m_2=1\therefore$ Tangent to the curve is perpendicular to line (ii).
$\therefore \quad m_1 \cdot m_2=-1m_1 \cdot 1=-1\begin{array}{cc}\Rightarrow & m_1=-1 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 x-3=-1 \\ \Rightarrow & 2 x=2 \\ \Rightarrow & x=1\end{array}
\therefore \quad y=(1)^2-3 \times1+2y=0\therefore$ Point of tangent drawn $=(1,0)$

6282.subject: Mathematics
6282.text: Let $f\left(x\right) = \left(x - a\right)\left(x - b\right) - \left(\dfrac{a + b}{2}\right).$ If $f  \left(x\right) = 0$ has both non-negative roots, then the minimum value of $f\left(x\right)$
6282.sol:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \left(x - a\right)\left(x - b\right) - \left(\dfrac{a + b}{2}\right)$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {x}^{2} - \left(a + b\right)x - \left(\dfrac{a + b}{2}\right)$

Let $\alpha \text{ and } \beta$ be the roots of $f\left(x\right)$.

$\alpha, \beta > 0$ where the minimum is obtained i.e. $\dfrac{- b}{2a} > 0$

$\dfrac{a + b}{2} > 0 ⇒ a + b > 0 . . . \left(i\right)$

Now, 

${x}^{2} - \left(a + b\right)x - \left(\dfrac{a + b}{2}\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{\left(a + b\right) \pm \sqrt{{\left(a + b\right)}^{2} - 4\left(ab + \dfrac{a + b}{2}\right)}}{2}$

Roots are non-negative, so

$\dfrac{\left(a + b\right) \pm \sqrt{{\left(a - b\right)}^{2} + 2\left(a + b\right)}}{2} \ge 0$

$⇒ \left(a + b\right) \pm \sqrt{{\left(a - b\right)}^{2} + 2\left(a + b\right)} \ge 0$

$⇒ {\left(a + b\right)}^{2} \ge {\left(a - b\right)}^{2} + 2\left(a + b\right)$

$⇒ \left(a + b\right) \le 2ab . . . \left(ii\right)$

By $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$, we have

$0 < \left(a + b\right) \le 2ab$

Minimum value$= \dfrac{- D}{4a}$

 $= - \left\{\dfrac{{\left(a - b\right)}^{2} + 2\left(a + b\right)}{4}\right\}$

   $= - \left\{\dfrac{{\left(a - b\right)}^{2} + 4ab}{4}\right\}$

   $= - \left\{\dfrac{{\left(a + b\right)}^{2}}{4}\right\}$

Therefore, $f\left(x\right) \ge - \dfrac{{\left(a + b\right)}^{2}}{4}$.

Probability of $B$ speaking truth is $P\left(B\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Probability of $B$ not speaking truth is $P\left(\overset{¯}{B}\right) = 1 - P\left(B\right) = 1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Probability that they contradict each other is$= P \left(B\right). P \left(A\right) + P \left(A\right). P\left(B\right)$

11627.subject: Mathematics
11627.text: The value of the sum $1 \times 2 \times 3+2 \times 3 \times 4+3 \times 4 \times 5+\ldots$ upto $n$ terms is equal to
11627.sol:
Let given series be
$S=1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3+2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4+3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5+\ldots n$ terms
Now, general term $\begin{aligned}& T_n=\{1+(n-1) \cdot1\}\{2+(n-1) \cdot1\}\{3+(n-1) \cdot1\} \\
& =(1+n-1)(2+n-1)(3+n-1) \\
& =n(n+1)(n+2) \\
& =n\left( n^2+3 n+2\right) \\
& =n³+3 n²+2 n
\end{aligned} Now, \begin{aligned}& \text{ Sum$ of $the series } \mathrm{S}=\sum T_n=\sum\left( n^3+3 n²+2 n\right) \\
& =\sum n^3+3 \sum n^2+2 \sum n \\
& =\frac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}+\frac{3 n(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}+\frac{2 n(n+1)}{2}\\
& =\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}+(2 n+1)+2\right]
\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & =\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\left[\frac{n^2+n+4 n+2+4}{2}\right] \\ & =\frac{n(n+1)\left(n^2+5 n+6\right)}{4} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{S}=\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)}{4}\end{aligned}$

20334.subject: Chemistry
20334.text: Identify the final product $[Z]$ formed when Chlorobenzene undergoes the given series of reactions:
20334.sol:
The reaction sequence begins with the Friedel-Crafts alkylation of chlorobenzene with methyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_{3}$. Chlorobenzene is ortho/para directing, and the para-isomer is the major product due to steric hindrance at the ortho position. Thus, $[W]$ is 1-chloro-4-methylbenzene (p-chlorotoluene).

Next, $[W]$ reacts with $Cl_{2}$ in the presence of UV light. This is a free-radical substitution reaction that occurs at the benzylic position. Therefore, $[X]$ is 1-chloro-4-(chloromethyl)benzene (p-chlorobenzyl chloride).

Then, $[X]$ reacts with alcoholic $KCN$ and heat. This is a nucleophilic substitution reaction where the benzylic chloride is replaced by a cyanide group, yielding $[Y]$, which is 2-(4-chlorophenyl)acetonitrile.

Finally, the hydrolysis of the nitrile $[Y]$ with excess dilute $HCl$ converts the $-CN$ group into a carboxylic acid group $-COOH$. Thus, the final product $[Z]$ is 2-(4-chlorophenyl)acetic acid, which corresponds to the structure shown in the first option.

Answer:

20404.text:
Given below are 4 reactions. Two of these reactions will give product which is an equimolar mixture of the d and 1 forms. Identify these 2 reactions.
[A] 2- Methylpropene + $\mathrm{HI} \rightarrow$ ---------
[B] But-1-ene + $\mathrm{HBr} \rightarrow$ -----------
[C] 3-Methylbut-1-ene + $\mathrm{HI} \rightarrow$ -----------
[D] 3- Phenylpropene + $\mathrm{HBr}$ (Peroxide) $\rightarrow -----------$
20404.sol:
For a racemic (equimolar d and l) mixture, the product must have a chiral center formed from an achiral reactant via a planar intermediate (carbocation).

[A] 2-Methylpropene + HI \to Markovnikov addition gives tertiary carbocation \to 2-iodo-2-methylpropane $CH_3 - C(I)(CH_3)_2$. Central carbon has three identical methyl groups \to achiral. No racemic mixture.

[B] But-1-ene + HBr \to Markovnikov addition gives secondary carbocation \to 2-bromobutane $ CH_3 - CHBr - CH_2CH_3$. C-2 is bonded to H, Br, $CH_3$, and $C_2H_5\to$ chiral center. Attack from either face equally probable \to racemic mixture.

[C] 3-Methylbut-1-ene + HI \to Markovnikov addition gives secondary carbocation $ CH_3 - CH^+ - CH(CH_3)_2\to$ iodide attacks to give 2-iodo-3-methylbutane with chiral center at C-2 \to racemic mixture.

[D] 3-Phenylpropene + HBr (peroxide) \to anti-Markovnikov (radical) addition \to Br adds to terminal carbon \to 1-bromo-3-phenylpropane $ C_6H_5 - CH_2 - CH_2 - CH_2Br\to$ no chiral center \to achiral.

Reactions giving racemic mixture: B and C. Answer: (1)

20878.subject: Chemistry
20878.text: When the expansion of a gas occurs in vaccum and at constant volume, then
20878.sol:
For any thermodynamic process, the first law of thermodynamics is given by $\Delta U = q + w$, where $w$ is the work done on the system.

In the case of expansion in a vacuum, the external pressure $P_{ext} = 0$. Since $w = -\int P_{ext} dV$, the work done $w = 0$.

At constant volume, the change in volume $dV = 0$, which also implies $w = 0$.

Substituting $w = 0$ into the first law equation, we get $\Delta U = q$.

Since the process occurs at constant volume, the heat exchanged is denoted as $q_V$. Therefore, $\Delta U = q_V$.

Answer: $\Delta U=q V$

20950.subject: Mathematics
20950.text: The most economical proportion of the height of a covered box of fixed volume whose base is a rectangle with one side three times as long as the other, is
options: Equal to shorter side of base
20950.sol:
Let the sides of the rectangular base be $x$ and $3x$. Let the height of the box be $h$.

The volume $V$ of the box is given by $V = (x)(3x)(h) = 3x^2 h$. Since $V$ is fixed, $h = \dfrac{V}{3x^2}$.

The surface area $S$ of the covered box is $S = 2(length \times width + width \times height + height \times length) = 2(3x^2 + 3xh + xh) = 2(3x^2 + 4xh)$.

Substituting $h = \dfrac{V}{3x^2}$ into the surface area equation:

$S = 6x^2 + 8x \left( \dfrac{V}{3x^2} \right) = 6x^2 + \dfrac{8V}{3x}$.

To minimize $S$, differentiate with respect to $x$ and set to zero:

$\dfrac{dS}{dx} = 12x - \dfrac{8V}{3x^2} = 0$.

$12x = \dfrac{8V}{3x^2} \Rightarrow 36x^3 = 8V \Rightarrow V = \dfrac{36x^3}{8} = \dfrac{9x^3}{2}$.

Substitute $V$ back into the expression for $h$:

$h = \dfrac{9x^3 / 2}{3x^2} = \dfrac{3x}{2}$.

The height $h$ is $\dfrac{3}{2}$ times the shorter side of the base $x$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2} \times$ shorter side of base

20997.sol:

For increasing function, $f^{\prime}(x) > 0\Rightarrow \quad(x-3)(x+2) < 0\Rightarrow \quad x < 3$ and $x > -2\Rightarrow \quad-2 < x < 3$
Hence, function $f(x)$ is increasing $\operatorname{in}(-2,3)$ interval.

21450.text: The domain of the function $\sin ^{-1}  \left(x²-4\right) is$
21450.sol:
The domain of the function $f(x) = \sin^{-1}(u)$ is defined by the condition $-1 \le u \le 1$.

For the given function $f(x) = \sin^{-1}(x^2 - 4)$, we must have $-1 \le x^2 - 4 \le 1$.

Adding 4 to all parts of the inequality:

$3 \le x^2 \le 5$.

This inequality implies two conditions: $x^2 \ge 3$ and $x^2 \le 5$.

Solving $x^2 \ge 3$ gives $x \in (-\infty, -\sqrt{3}] \cup [\sqrt{3}, \infty)$.

Solving $x^2 \le 5$ gives $x \in [-\sqrt{5}, \sqrt{5}]$.

The domain is the intersection of these two sets:

$([-\infty, -\sqrt{3}] \cup [\sqrt{3}, \infty]) \cap [-\sqrt{5}, \sqrt{5}] = [-\sqrt{5}, -\sqrt{3}] \cup [\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{5}]$.

Answer: $[-\sqrt{5},-\sqrt{3}] \cup[\sqrt{3}, \sqrt{5}]$

21892.subject: Mathematics
21892.text: If A and B are two events such that $P(\bar{A})=0.3, P(B)=0.4, P(A \cap \bar{B})=0.5$, then find the value of $P(B / A \cup \bar{B})$
21892.sol:
Given $P(\bar{A}) = 0.3$, we have $P(A) = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7$.

Given $P(A \cap \bar{B}) = 0.5$, we use the identity $P(A \cap \bar{B}) = P(A) - P(A \cap B)$.

$0.5 = 0.7 - P(A \cap B) \Rightarrow P(A \cap B) = 0.2$.

We need to find $P(B | A \cup \bar{B}) = \dfrac{P(B \cap (A \cup \bar{B}))}{P(A \cup \bar{B})}$.

The numerator is $P((B \cap A) \cup (B \cap \bar{B})) = P(B \cap A) \cup \emptyset = P(A \cap B) = 0.2$.

The denominator is $P(A \cup \bar{B}) = P(A) + P(\bar{B}) - P(A \cap \bar{B})$.

Since $P(B) = 0.4$, $P(\bar{B}) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$.

$P(A \cup \bar{B}) = 0.7 + 0.6 - 0.5 = 0.8$.

Therefore, $P(B | A \cup \bar{B}) = \dfrac{0.2}{0.8} = \dfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$.

Answer: $0.25$

22011.text: If $S=\dfrac{2^2-1}{2}+\dfrac{3^2-2}{6}+\dfrac{4^2-3}{12}+\ldots$ upto 10 terms, then $S$ is equal to
22011.sol:
The general term $T_n$ of the series is given by $T_n = \dfrac{(n+1)^2 - n}{n(n+1)}$.

Simplifying the numerator: $(n+1)^2 - n = n^2 + 2n + 1 - n = n^2 + n + 1$.

Thus, $T_n = \dfrac{n^2 + n + 1}{n(n+1)} = \dfrac{n(n+1) + 1}{n(n+1)} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{n(n+1)}$.

Using partial fractions, $\dfrac{1}{n(n+1)} = \dfrac{1}{n} - \dfrac{1}{n+1}$.

Therefore, $T_n = 1 + \dfrac{1}{n} - \dfrac{1}{n+1}$.

The sum of 10 terms is $S = \sum_{n=1}^{10} T_n = \sum_{n=1}^{10} (1 + \dfrac{1}{n} - \dfrac{1}{n+1})$.

$S = \sum_{n=1}^{10} 1 + \sum_{n=1}^{10} (\dfrac{1}{n} - \dfrac{1}{n+1})$.

The first part is $10 \times 1 = 10$.

The second part is a telescoping sum: $(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}) + (\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{3}) + \ldots + (\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{11}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{11} = \dfrac{10}{11}$.

$S = 10 + \dfrac{10}{11} = \dfrac{110 + 10}{11} = \dfrac{120}{11}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{120}{11}$

22937.text: A vessel of volume $27 \times 10^4$ cc, contains a mixture of Hydrogen (molar mass $= 2\ g\ mol^{-1}$) and oxygen (molar mass $= 32\ g\ mol^{-1}$) gas at standard temperature and pressure. If the mass of hydrogen is 16 g, find the mass of oxygen gas contained in the vessel.
22937.sol:
Volume of the vessel, $V = 27 \times 10^4$ cc $= 270$ L

At STP, the volume of $1$ mole of an ideal gas is $22.4$ L.

Total number of moles in the mixture, $n = \dfrac{270}{22.4} \approx 12.054$

Number of moles of hydrogen, $n_{H_2} = \dfrac{16}{2} = 8$

Number of moles of oxygen, $n_{O_2} = n - n_{H_2} = 12.054 - 8 = 4.054$

Mass of oxygen, $m_{O_2} = n_{O_2} \times 32 = 4.054 \times 32 \approx 129.7$ g

Answer: $129.7$ g

25400.text:
Let $f: \left[- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function such that $f\left(0\right) = 1$ and ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}f\left(t\right)dt = 0$

Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: The equation $f\left(x\right) - 3cos3x = 0$ has at least one solution in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$
The equation $f\left(x\right) - 3sin3x = - \dfrac{6}{\pi}$ has at least one solution in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$
25400.sol:
(A) Let $g\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) - 3cos3x$

Now

${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}g\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}f\left(x\right)dx - 3{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}cos3xdx$

$= 0 - {\left[sin3x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} = 0$

Hence $g\left(x\right) = 0$ has a root in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

(B) Let $h\left(x\right) = f\left(x\right) - 3sin3x + \dfrac{6}{\pi}$

Now

${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}h\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}f\left(x\right)dx - 3{∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}sin3xdx + {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\dfrac{6}{\pi}dx$

$= 0 - {\left[- cos3x\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} + {\left[\dfrac{6x}{\pi}\right]}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}$

$= 0 - 2 + 2 = 0$

Hence $h\left(x\right) = 0$has a root in $\left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

(C) $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x{∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt}{1 - {e}^{{x}^{2}}}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\mathop{\mathop{\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{1 - {e}^{{x}^{2}}}\right) \times}_{⏟}}_{- 1}\mathop{\mathop{\left(\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}f( t )dt}{x}\right)}_{⏟}}_{Apply{L}^{'}hospitalrule}\right)$

$= - 1\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{1} = - 1$

(D) $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{( sinx ) {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt}{{x}^{2}}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\mathop{\mathop{\left(\dfrac{sinx}{x}\right)}_{⏟}}_{1} \times \mathop{\mathop{\left(\dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{x}f( t )dt}{x}\right)}_{⏟}}_{Apply{L}^{'}hospitalrule}\right)$

$= 1\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{1} = 1$

26486.subject: Physics
26486.text: On a frictionless horizontal plane, a bob of mass $m = 0 . 1kg$ is attached to a spring with natural length ${l}_{0} = 0 . 1m$. The spring constant is ${k}_{1} = 0 . 009N{m}^{- 1}$ when the length of the spring $l > {l}_{0}$ and is ${k}_{2} = 0 . 016N{m}^{- 1}$ when $l < {l}_{0}$. Initially the bob is released from $l = 0 . 15m$. Assume that Hooke's law remains valid throughout the motion. If the time period of the full oscillation is $T = \left(n\pi\right)s$, then the integer closest to $n$ is _______.
26486.sol:
Angular frequency for different values of spring constant will be given by, ${\omega}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{1}}{m}}$ and ${\omega}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{k}_{2}}{m}}$

Time period for a spring of fix spring constant, $k$ is given by, $= 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$.

As per question, spring constant is having different values, hence we will have to find half of the time period for the given parts, first for the right half part of the oscillations & next for the left half part of the oscillation from the mean position.

$∴$ Time period $= \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{k}_{1}}} + \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{{k}_{2}}}$

$= \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{0 . 1}{0 . 009}} + \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{0 . 1}{0 . 016}}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{0 . 3} + \dfrac{\pi}{0 . 4}$

$= \pi \times \left(\dfrac{4 + 3}{12}\right) \times 10$

$= \dfrac{70}{12}\pi$

28368.subject: Chemistry
28368.text:
Match List I with List II

List II List II
(A) Tranquilizers (I) Anti blood clotting
(B) Aspirin (II) Salvarsan
(C) Antibiotic (III) Antidepressant drugs
(D) Antiseptic (IV) Soframicine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
28368.sol:
Tranquilizers are a class of chemical compounds used for the treatment of stress and mild or even severe mental diseases. For example, noradrenaline is one of the neurotransmitters that play a role in mood changes. If the level of noradrenaline is low for some reason, then the signal-sending activity becomes low, and the person suffers from depression. In such situations, antidepressant drugs are required.

Aspirin inhibits the synthesis of chemicals known as prostaglandins which stimulate inflammation in the tissue and cause pain. These drugs are effective in relieving skeletal pain such as that due to arthritis. These drugs have many other effects such as reducing fever (antipyretic) and preventing platelet coagulation. Because of its anti-blood clotting action, aspirin finds use in the prevention of heart attacks.

Antibiotics are used as drugs to treat infections because of their low toxicity for humans and animals. Paul Ehrlich, a German bacteriologist, investigated arsenic-based structures in order to produce less toxic substances for the treatment of syphilis. He developed the medicine, arsphenamine, known as salvarsan.

Antiseptics are applied to the living tissues such as wounds, cuts, ulcers and diseased skin surfaces. Examples are furacine, soframicine, etc.

So, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

31178.text:
Match List-I and List-II.

List-I List-II
A. Elastomeric polymer I. Urea formaldehyde resin
B. Fibre polymer II. Polystyrene
C. Thermosetting polymer III. Polyester
D. Thermoplastic polymer IV. Neoprene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
31178.sol:
(A) Rubber is a natural polymer and possesses elastic properties. It is also termed as elastomeric polymer. Neoprene is a family of synthetic rubbers that are produced by the polymerization of chloroprene. So, the correct matching of elastomeric polymer is neoprene.

(B) Polyesters are the polycondensation products of dicarboxylic acids and diols. Dacron or terylene is the best-known example of polyester. Dacron fibre is crease-resistant and is used in blending with cotton and wool fibres and also as glass reinforcing materials in safety helmets, etc. So, the correct matching of fibre polymer is polyester.

(C) Thermosetting polymer which cannot be reused or remoulded. Urea formaldehyde resin and phenol-formaldehyde resins are the thermosetting polymers.

(D) Thermoplastics can soften upon heating and return to their original form on cooling. They are easily moulded and extruded into films, fibres and packaging. Polystyrene is an example of a thermoplastic polymer.

So the correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

31329.text:
Chlorine undergoes disproportionation in alkaline medium as shown below :
${aCl}_{2} ( g ) + {bOH}^{-} ( aq ) \to {cClO}^{-} ( aq ) + {dCl}^{-} ( aq ) + {eH}_{2}O ( l )$

The values of $a, b, c$ and $d$ in a balanced redox reaction are respectively :
31329.sol:
Chlorine undergoes disproportionation reaction in alkaline medium. It is the simultaneous oxidation-reduction. Chlorine is simultaneously reduced to chloride ion ${Cl}^{-}$ and is oxidised to  ${ClO}^{-}$  ion. Halogens (e.g. Cl) have a strong tendency to accept electrons, so they act as strong oxidising agents.

The reaction is as follows,

\(\Rightarrow \mathrm{Cl}_2 - 2 \mathrm{O} \mathrm{H}^- \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cl}^{-}+\mathrm{ClO}^{-}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\)

Hence the values of a,b,c,d are $1, 2, 1, 1 .$

35586.subject: Mathematics
35586.text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}-2 x-2}\right)$, is $(-\infty, \alpha] \cup[\beta, \gamma] \cup[\delta, \infty)$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta$ is equal to
35586.sol:
For $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{x^2-2x-2}\right)$ to be defined, we need $\left|\frac{1}{x^2-2x-2}\right| \leq 1$, i.e., $|x^2-2x-2| \geq 1$.
Case 1:
$x^2-2x-2 \geq 1 \Rightarrow x^2-2x-3 \geq 0$
$\Rightarrow (x-3)(x+1) \geq 0$
$\Rightarrow x \leq -1$ or $x \geq 3$.
Case 2:
$x^2-2x-2 \leq -1 \Rightarrow x^2-2x-1 \leq 0$
$\Rightarrow (x-1)^2 \leq 2$
$\Rightarrow 1-\sqrt{2} \leq x \leq 1+\sqrt{2}$.
Domain $= (-\infty, -1] \cup [1-\sqrt{2}, 1+\sqrt{2}] \cup [3, \infty)$.
So $\alpha = -1,\ \beta = 1-\sqrt{2},\ \gamma = 1+\sqrt{2},\ \delta = 3$.
$\alpha + \beta + \gamma + \delta = -1 + 1 - \sqrt{2} + 1 + \sqrt{2} + 3 = 4$.

35852.text: Which of the following statements is a tautology?
35852.sol:
Plotting the truth table of the following option we have,

$p$ $q$ $~ p$ $~ q$ $~ p ∨ q$
$T$ $T$ $F$ $F$ $T$
$T$ $F$ $F$ $T$ $F$
$F$ $T$ $T$ $F$ $T$
$F$ $F$ $T$ $T$ $T$

We know that, $A ⇒ B$ is only false when $A$ is true and $B$ is false, now using this rule and above table we will make truth table of options,

$\left(\left(~ p\right) ∨ q\right) ⇒ p$ $p ⇒ \left(\left(~ p\right) ∨ q\right)$ $\left(\left(~ p\right) ∨ q\right) ⇒ q$ $q ⇒ \left(\left(~ p\right) ∨ q\right)$
$T$ $T$ $T$ $T$
$T$ $F$ $T$ $T$
$F$ $T$ $T$ $T$
$F$ $T$ $F$ $T$

Hence $q ⇒ \left(\left(~ p\right) ∨ q\right)$ is tautology.

36231.text: Let a tangent to the curve ${y}^{2} = 24x$ meet the curve $xy = 2$ at the points $A$ and $B$. Then the mid-points of such line segments $AB$ lie on a parabola with the
36231.sol:
Given:

${y}^{2} = 24x$

Comparing with ${y}^{2} = 4ax$, we get

$4a = 24 ⇒ a = 6$

Also given $xy = 2$

Let any point $Q ≡ \left(a{t}^{2}, 2at\right) ≡ \left(6{t}^{2}, 12t\right)$ on the parabola.

Equation of tangent at $Q$ is

$12yt = 12\left(x + 6{t}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ yt = x + 6{t}^{2}$

$⇒ x - yt + 6{t}^{2} = 0 . . . . \left(i\right)$

Let mid-point of $AB$ be $P\left(h, k\right)$.

Equation of chord of hyperbola is

$\dfrac{xk + yh}{2} = hk$

$⇒ xk + hy - 2hk = 0 . . . \left(ii\right)$

Since, $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(ii\right)$ are same, so on comparing, we get

$\dfrac{k}{1} = \dfrac{h}{- t} = \dfrac{- 2hk}{6{t}^{2}}$

$⇒ t = - \dfrac{h}{k} \text{ and }$$\dfrac{h}{- t} = \dfrac{- 2hk}{6{t}^{2}} ⇒ t = \dfrac{k}{3}$

So,

$\dfrac{k}{3} = - \dfrac{h}{k}$

$⇒ {k}^{2} = - 3h$

Hence, locus is ${y}^{2} = - 3x$.

Therefore, directrix is $4x = 3$.

Length of latus rectum is $= 4a = 3$

$= 5 \times 5 \times 3 \times 8 + 5 \times 2 \times 5 \times 9 + 10 \times 10 + 5$

$= 600 + 450 + 100 + 5 = 1155$

Total no. of ways $= 1155$
No. of ways to form a committee having more women than men

probability$= \dfrac{105}{1155} = \dfrac{1}{11}$

37392.text: Let A be the set of all functions $f: \mathbf{Z} \rightarrow \mathbf{Z}$ and R be a relation on A such that $\mathrm{R}=\{(\mathrm{f}, \mathrm{g}): f(0)=\mathrm{g}(1)$ and $f(1)=\mathrm{g}(0)\}$. Then R is:
options: Symmetric and transitive but not reflective
Symmetric but neither reflective nor transitive
Reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
Transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric
37392.sol:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}=\{(\mathrm{f}, \mathrm{g}): \mathrm{f}(0)=\mathrm{g}(1) \text{$ and $} \mathrm{f}(1)=\mathrm{g}(0)\} \\ & \text{ Reflexive: }(\mathrm{f}, \mathrm{f}) \in \mathrm{R} \\ & =\mathrm{f}(0)=\mathrm{f}(1) \text{ and } \mathrm{f}(1)=\mathrm{f}(0) \rightarrow \text{ must hold } \\ & \Rightarrow \text{ but this is not true for all function }\end{aligned}$
so not reflexive
Symmetric: If $(\mathrm{f}, \mathrm{g}) \in \mathrm{R} \Rightarrow(\mathrm{g}, \mathrm{f}) \in \mathrm{R}$
Now, g(0)=f(1) and $g(1)=f(0) \rightarrow$ true
$\therefore$ symmetric
Transitive : $\operatorname{If}(\mathrm{f}, \mathrm{g}) \in \mathrm{R}$ and $(\mathrm{g}, \mathrm{h}) \in \mathrm{R}$
$\Rightarrow(\mathrm{f}, \mathrm{h}) \in \mathrm{R}$
Now $(f, g) \in R \Rightarrow f(0)=g(1)$ and f(1)=g(0)
$(\mathrm{g}, \mathrm{h}) \in \mathrm{R} \Rightarrow \mathrm{g}(0)=\mathrm{h}(1) and \mathrm{g}(1)=\mathrm{h}(0)$
For $(f, h) \in R$ we need $f(0)=h(1) and f(1)=h(0)$
Now $f(0)=g(1)=h(0) and f(1)=g(0)=h(1)$
Hence not transitive

44417.subject: Physics
44417.text:
A person driving car at a constant speed of $15m{s}^{- 1}$ is approaching a vertical wall. The person notices a change of $40Hz$ in the frequency of his car’s horn upon reflection from the wall. The frequency of horn is$_______Hz .$

(Given: Speed of sound: $30m{s}^{- 1}$)
44417.sol:
The formula to calculate the frequency $\left(f '\right)$ as heard by an observer with respect to the frequency $\left(f\right)$ produced from a source is given by

$f ' = \dfrac{v \pm {v}_{o}}{v ∓ {v}_{s}}f . . . . ( 1 )$

where, $v$ is the speed of sound in air, ${v}_{o}$ is the speed of the observer and ${v}_{s}$ is the speed of the source.

In the first situation, the source is the moving car and the observer is the wall. Hence, the frequency $\left({f}_{w}\right)$ as heard on the wall can be written as

$\begin{cases}{f}_{w} & = & \dfrac{v - 0}{v - {v}_{c}}f \\ & = & \dfrac{v}{v - {v}_{c}}f . . . . ( 2 )\end{cases}$

where, ${v}_{c}$ is the speed of the car.

In the second situation, when the sound reflects back from the wall, the source of sound is the wall and the observer is the car.

Hence, the frequency $\left({f}_{c}\right)$ of sound as heard by the car after the reflection is given by

$\begin{cases}{f}_{c} & = & \dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v - 0}{f}_{w} \\ & = & \dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v}{f}_{w} . . . . ( 3 )\end{cases}$

From equation (2) and (3), it follows that

$\begin{cases}{f}_{c} & = & \dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v} \times \dfrac{v}{v - {v}_{c}}f \\ & = & \dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v - {v}_{c}}f . . . . ( 4 )\end{cases}$

It is given in the problem that

${f}_{c} - f = 40 . . . . . ( 5 )$

Substitute the expression from equation (4) into equation (5) and solve to calculate the frequency of the horn.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{v + {v}_{c}}{v - {v}_{c}}f - f & = & 40 \\ & ⇒ & \dfrac{2{v}_{c}}{v - {v}_{c}}f = 40\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases} & ⇒ & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & f\end{cases}\begin{cases} & = & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & 40\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \dfrac{v - {v}_{c}}{2{v}_{c}}\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & = & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & 40\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \times\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \dfrac{330 - 15}{2 \times 15}\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & m\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & s\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & {}^{- 1}\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & = & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & 420\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & m\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & \end{cases}\begin{cases} & & s\end{cases}\begin{cases} & & {}^{- 1}\end{cases}$

44554.subject: Physics
44554.text: A body of mass $1$ kg moves along a straight line with a velocity $v = 2x^2$. The work done by the body during displacement from $x = 0$ to $5$ m is __________ J.
44554.sol:
Given mass $m = 1$ kg and velocity $v = 2x^2$.

According to the work-energy theorem, the work done by the net force is equal to the change in kinetic energy of the body.

$W = \Delta K = K_f - K_i$

At $x = 0$ m, initial velocity $v_i = 2(0)^2 = 0$ m/s.

At $x = 5$ m, final velocity $v_f = 2(5)^2 = 50$ m/s.

Initial kinetic energy $K_i = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_i^2 = 0$ J.

Final kinetic energy $K_f = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_f^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times (50)^2 = 1250$ J.

Work done $W = 1250 - 0 = 1250$ J.

Answer: $1250$

44617.subject: Physics
44617.text:
A hollow spherical ball of uniform density rolls up a curved surface with an initial velocity $3m{s}^{- 1}$ (as shown in figure). Maximum height with respect to the initial position covered by it will be _____ $cm$
(take, $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
44617.sol:
The total kinetic energy of the ball at the bottom of the curve can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}K & = & \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}M{R}^{2}{\omega}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}M{\left(R\omega\right)}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}M{v}^{2}\left[∵ v = \omegaR\right] \\ & = & \dfrac{5}{6}M{v}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the potential energy acquired by the ball when it attains the maximum height is given by

$U = Mgh . . . \left(2\right)$

Equate equation (1) and (2) and simplify to obtain the required height.

$\begin{cases}Mgh & = & \dfrac{5}{6}M{v}^{2} \\ & ⇒ & h = \dfrac{5{v}^{2}}{6g} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required height attained by the ball.
$\begin{cases}h & = & \dfrac{5 \times {\left(3m{s}^{- 1}\right)}^{2}}{6 \times 10m{s}^{- 2}} \\ & = & 0 . 75m \times \dfrac{100cm}{1m} \\ & = & 75cm\end{cases}$

Because it is odourless, invisible, that is why, it is widely used in domestic refrigerators and cold storage facilities. It is calculated that the depletion of ozone layer by $1 \%$ results in an increase in the incidence of skin cancer by $5 \% to 7 \%$.

46377.text: The lower end of capillary tube is immresed in mercury. The level of mercury in the tube is found to be 2 cm below the outer level. If the same tube is immersed in water, upto what height will the water rise in the capillary?
46377.sol:
Given data:
Level of mercury in the tube is, \(\mathrm{h}^{\prime}=2 \mathrm{~cm}\).
Level of mercury in the tube is given as:
\(\mathrm{h}^{\prime}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T}^{\prime} \cos \theta^{\prime}}{\mathrm{r} \rho^{\prime} \mathrm{g}} . \quad \ldots (1)\)
where \(\rho^{\prime}\) is the density of mercury.
Level of water in the tube is given as:
\(\mathrm{h}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T} \cos \theta}{\mathrm{r} \rho \mathrm{g}} \quad \ldots (2)\)
where \(\rho\) is the density of water.
Here, the same capillary is immersed in both the liquids hence, the radius of the capillary is same i.e. \(r\)
Using the standard values for variables and taking \(\theta^{\prime}=135^{\circ}\), in equation (1) gives:
\(\begin{aligned}
& 2=\frac{2(484.5) \cos 135^{\circ}}{r(13.6)(980)} \\
& r=\frac{685.083}{(26656)} \\
& r=0.025 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}\)
Using value of \(r\) and \(\theta=0^{\circ}\) in equation (2), gives:
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{h}=\frac{2(72.7) \cos ^{\circ}}{(0.025)(1)(980)} \\
& \mathrm{h}=\frac{145.4}{(24.5)} \\
& \mathrm{h}=5.9 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}\)

55117.text:
Identify the reagent 'R' used in the following reaction
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{R}}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} + \text{HCl}$
55117.sol:
The given reaction is the conversion of benzoyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}$) to benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$).

This transformation is known as the Rosenmund reduction.

The reagent used for this reaction is hydrogen gas in the presence of a palladium catalyst supported on barium sulfate ($\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$).

The barium sulfate acts as a catalytic poison that partially deactivates the palladium, preventing the further reduction of the newly formed aldehyde into an alcohol.

Thus, the reagent 'R' is $\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$.

Answer: $\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$

56433.subject: Chemistry
56433.text: Which of the following sets of ligands does NOT contain ambident ligand in it?
56433.sol:
An ambidentate ligand is a ligand that has more than one type of donor atom and can bind to the central metal ion through any of these different donor atoms.

Examples of ambidentate ligands include $\text{NO}_2^-$ (which can bind through N or O) and $\text{NCS}^-$ (which can bind through N or S).

Checking the given options:
Option 1 contains $\text{NO}_2^-$ and $\text{NCS}^-$, both of which are ambidentate ligands.
Option 2 contains $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ (binds only through O), ethylene diamine (binds only through N), and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (binds only through O). None of these are ambidentate ligands.
Option 3 contains $\text{NO}_2^-$, which is an ambidentate ligand.
Option 4 contains $\text{NCS}^-$, which is an ambidentate ligand.

Therefore, the set containing $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$, ethylene diamine, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ does not contain any ambidentate ligand.

56438.subject: Chemistry
56438.text: Which from following complexes does NOT obey EAN rule?
56438.sol:
Effective Atomic Number analysis determines which complex violates the noble gas electron count rule.

The EAN equals the sum of metal valence electrons and ligand-donated electrons, aiming for Kr (36), Xe (54), or Rn (86). For monodentate ligands: $\text{EAN} = Z_{\text{metal}} - \text{oxidation state} + 2 \times \text{number of ligands}$.

For $\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6^{3+}$: Co atomic number 27, oxidation state +3 gives 24 valence electrons; 6 $\mathrm{NH}_3$ donate 12 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 24 + 12 = 36$, satisfying the rule.

For $\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{CO})_6$: Cr atomic number 24, oxidation state 0 gives 24 valence electrons; 6 CO donate 12 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 24 + 12 = 36$, satisfying the rule.

For $\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4^{2+}$: Zn atomic number 30, oxidation state +2 gives 28 valence electrons; 4 $\mathrm{NH}_3$ donate 8 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 28 + 8 = 36$, satisfying the rule.

For $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4^{2+}$: Cu atomic number 29, oxidation state +2 gives 27 valence electrons; 4 $\mathrm{NH}_3$ donate 8 electrons. $\text{EAN} = 27 + 8 = 35 \neq 36$, violating the rule.

The complex that does not obey the EAN rule is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

56638.text: What is the value of spin only magnetic moment for $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ in BM?

The atomic number of $\text{Cu}$ is $29$.

The spin only magnetic moment is given by $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$.

57997.subject: Chemistry
57997.text: Identify conjugate acid and conjugate base for $\mathrm{HCO}_3{ }^{-}$ ion respectively
57997.sol:
To determine the conjugate acid and conjugate base of $\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}$, consider its amphoteric nature—it can either accept or donate a proton ($\mathrm{H}^{+}$).

As a base, $\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}$ accepts $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ to form its conjugate acid: $\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-} + \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$.

As an acid, $\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}$ donates $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ to form its conjugate base: $\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}^{+} + \mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}$.

The conjugate acid is $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ and the conjugate base is $\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}$.

Evaluating the options:
Option A: $\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ (incorrect order)
Option B: $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ (incorrect conjugate base)
Option C: $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ (both incorrect)
Option D: $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ and $\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}$ (correct).

The answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

60201.subject: Mathematics
60201.text: The coordinates of the points on the curve $4y = x^2$ that are nearest to the point $(0,5)$ are...
60201.sol:
Let the point on the curve be $(x, y)$.

The square of the distance $S$ between $(x, y)$ and $(0, 5)$ is given by:

$S = x^2 + (y - 5)^2$

Since the point lies on the curve $4y = x^2$, we substitute $x^2 = 4y$ into the equation for $S$:

$S = 4y + (y - 5)^2$

$S = y^2 - 6y + 25$

To find the minimum distance, we differentiate $S$ with respect to $y$ and equate it to zero:

$\dfrac{dS}{dy} = 2y - 6 = 0$

$y = 3$

Since $\dfrac{d^2S}{dy^2} = 2 > 0$, the distance is minimum at $y = 3$.

Substituting $y = 3$ in $x^2 = 4y$, we get:

$x^2 = 12 \Rightarrow x = \pm 2\sqrt{3}$

The points on the curve nearest to $(0, 5)$ are $(2\sqrt{3}, 3)$ and $(-2\sqrt{3}, 3)$.

Answer: $(-2\sqrt{3}, 3)$

61718.sol:
Given $y = \log_e x^3 + 3 \sin^{-1} x + k x^2$, simplifying the logarithm yields $y = 3 \log_e x + 3 \sin^{-1} x + k x^2$.

Differentiating, $y' = 3 \cdot \frac{1}{x} + 3 \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} + 2k x = \frac{3}{x} + \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} + 2k x$.

At $x = \frac{1}{2}$, $y'\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{3}{1/2} + \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}} + 2k \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 6 + \frac{3}{\sqrt{3/4}} + k = 6 + \frac{3}{\sqrt{3}/2} + k = 6 + \frac{6}{\sqrt{3}} + k$.

Rationalizing, $\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = 2 \sqrt{3}$, so $y'\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 6 + 2 \sqrt{3} + k$.

Given $y'\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 2 \sqrt{3}$, equating gives $6 + 2 \sqrt{3} + k = 2 \sqrt{3}$, hence $k = -6$.

61721.sol:
Given the implicit equation $x^{\frac{2}{5}} + y^{\frac{2}{5}} = a^{\frac{2}{5}}$, we seek the derivative $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, and applying the chain rule to the $y$ term:

$\frac{2}{5}x^{-\frac{3}{5}} + \frac{2}{5}y^{-\frac{3}{5}} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$

Solving for $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$:

$\frac{2}{5}y^{-\frac{3}{5}} \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = -\frac{2}{5}x^{-\frac{3}{5}}$

Dividing both sides by common factors and simplifying:

$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = -\frac{y^{\frac{3}{5}}}{x^{\frac{3}{5}}}$

This may be expressed as $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = -\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{\frac{3}{5}}$, which matches option D.

65185.subject: Mathematics
65185.text: Let $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{c}$ be unit vectors at an angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ with each other. If $(\bar{a} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})) \cdot(\bar{a} \times \bar{c})=5$, then $\left[\begin{array}{lll}\bar{a} & \bar{b} & \bar{c}\end{array}$\right]=
65185.sol:
The given equation is $(\bar{a} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})) \cdot(\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) = 5$.

Using the BAC-CAB identity, $\bar{a} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c}$.

Substituting into the original equation yields $[(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c}] \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) = 5$.

Expanding the dot product gives $(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})[\bar{b} \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{c})] - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})[\bar{c} \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{c})] = 5$.

Since $\bar{c} \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) = 0$ (as two identical vectors in a scalar triple product yield zero), the second term vanishes, simplifying to $(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})[\bar{b} \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{c})] = 5$.

Given $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{c}$ are unit vectors with an angle of $\frac{\pi}{3}$, $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = 1 \cdot 1 \cdot \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}$.

Substituting, $\frac{1}{2}[\bar{b} \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{c})] = 5$, so $\bar{b} \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) = 10$.

This expression equals the scalar triple product $[\bar{b} \bar{a} \bar{c}]$, which is related to $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]$ by a sign change: $[\bar{b} \bar{a} \bar{c}] = -[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]$.

Thus, $-[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}] = 10$, giving $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}] = -10$.

The correct option is B, and the final answer is $\boxed{-10}$.

65625.sol:
Alternating Current in Secondary Coil

For an ideal transformer, power is conserved between the primary and secondary coils.

The power supplied to the primary equals the power delivered by the secondary:

Substitute $P = 4400 \text{W}$ and $V_s = 3300 \text{V}$:

Solving for $I_s$:

$I_s = \frac{4400}{3300} = \frac{44}{33} = \frac{4}{3} \text{A}$

66560.sol:
Photoelectron emission occurs when incident radiation energy $E$ exceeds or equals the work function $\Phi$ of the metal. Comparing the given $E = 2.41 \, \text{eV}$ with each work function:

For Caesium: $\Phi_{\text{Cs}} = 2.14 \, \text{eV}$, so $2.41 \ge 2.14$.

For Potassium: $\Phi_{\text{K}} = 2.30 \, \text{eV}$, so $2.41 \ge 2.30$.

For Sodium: $\Phi_{\text{Na}} = 2.75 \, \text{eV}$, so $2.41 < 2.75$.

Emission occurs for Caesium and Potassium, but not Sodium.

66784.text: A coil having ' N ' turns and resistance ' R ' $\Omega$ is connected to a galvanometer of resistance '6R' $\Omega$. The magnetic flux linked with this coil changes from $\phi_1$ weber to $\phi_2$ weber in time ' $t$ ' second. The induced current in the circuit is
66784.sol:
The induced current $I$ is determined by the induced EMF and the total circuit resistance.

With coil resistance $R$ and galvanometer resistance $6R$ in series, the total resistance is $R_{\text{total}} = R + 6R = 7R$.

Faraday's law gives the magnitude of induced EMF as $|\varepsilon| = N \frac{\phi_2 - \phi_1}{t}$ for flux change $\phi_2 - \phi_1$ over time $t$.

Applying Ohm's law yields $I = \frac{|\varepsilon|}{R_{\text{total}}} = \frac{N(\phi_2 - \phi_1)}{7Rt}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

68703.subject: Physics
68703.text: The displacement of particle in S.H.M. is $x=A \cos (\omega t+\pi / 6)$. Its speed will be maximum at time $\left(\operatorname{Sin} 90^{\circ}=1\right)$
68703.sol:
The displacement of the particle undergoing simple harmonic motion is given by

$x = A \cos \left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)$

Differentiation yields the velocity function:

$v = -A\omega \sin \left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)$

where speed is the magnitude $|v|$, requiring $|\sin (\omega t + \pi/6)| = 1$ for maximum value.

This maximum first occurs at the smallest positive argument where $\sin(\theta) = 1$, corresponding to $\theta = \pi/2$. Setting $\omega t + \pi/6 = \pi/2$ gives $\omega t = \pi/3$, yielding $t = \pi/(3\omega)$.

Maximum speed is achieved at time $t = \frac{\pi}{3\omega}$ $\text{s}$.

Answer: A

69918.subject: Physics
69918.text: A thermodynamic system is compressed adiabatically, then its temperature
69918.sol:
In an adiabatic process, there is no heat exchange with the surroundings, so $dQ = 0$.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $dQ = dU + dW$.

Substituting $dQ = 0$, we get $dU = -dW$.

During compression, work is done on the system, which means the work done by the system $dW$ is negative ($dW < 0$).

Therefore, $dU = -(-\text{positive value}) > 0$.

Since the internal energy $U$ increases and internal energy is directly proportional to temperature ($dU = nC_v dT$), the temperature of the system increases.

70397.text: The equation of a wave on a string of linear mass density $0.02\ \text{kg m}^{-1}$ is $Y = 0.01\sin\left[2\pi\left(\dfrac{t}{0.02} - \dfrac{x}{0.50}\right)\right]$ m. The tension in the string is
70397.sol:
The given wave equation is $Y = 0.01\sin\left[2\pi\left(\dfrac{t}{0.02} - \dfrac{x}{0.50}\right)\right]$ m.

Comparing this with the standard wave equation $Y = A\sin(\omega t - kx)$, we get:

$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{0.02} = 100\pi\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$

$k = \dfrac{2\pi}{0.50} = 4\pi\ \text{m}^{-1}$

The wave velocity $v$ is given by:

$v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{100\pi}{4\pi} = 25\ \text{m s}^{-1}$

The velocity of a transverse wave on a string is also given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, where $T$ is the tension and $\mu$ is the linear mass density.

Given $\mu = 0.02\ \text{kg m}^{-1}$.

$T = \mu v^2 = 0.02 \times (25)^2$

$T = 0.02 \times 625 = 12.50\ \text{N}$

Answer: $12.50$ N

71195.subject: Biology
71195.text: Which one of the following hormones is NOT involved in the process of parturition in human?
71195.sol:
Parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism involving cortisol, estrogens, and oxytocin.

The signals for parturition originate from the fully developed fetus and the placenta. The fetal pituitary secretes ACTH, which stimulates the fetal adrenal glands to secrete corticosteroids (cortisol). Corticosteroids cross the placenta and alter the estrogen to progesterone ratio, increasing prostaglandin synthesis and stimulating uterine contractions.

The mild uterine contractions (fetal ejection reflex) trigger the release of oxytocin from the maternal posterior pituitary, which causes stronger uterine contractions, leading to the expulsion of the baby.

Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is secreted by the placenta during early pregnancy to maintain the corpus luteum and stimulate it to secrete progesterone and estrogen. It is not involved in the process of parturition.

Answer: hCG

71395.subject: Biology
71395.text: In a monohybrid cross between pure tall pea plant with pure dwarf pea plant, how many types of genotypes are found in the $F_2$ generation ?
71395.sol:
A pure tall pea plant has the genotype $TT$ and a pure dwarf pea plant has the genotype $tt$.

The cross between them (TT \times tt$) produces $F_1$ offspring with the genotype $Tt$ (heterozygous tall).

Selfing the $F_1$ generation (Tt \times Tt$) yields the $F_2$ generation.

The genotypes produced in the $F_2$ generation are $TT$, $Tt$, and $tt$.

Thus, there are $3$ types of genotypes found in the $F_2$ generation.

Answer: 3

71820.subject: Chemistry
71820.text: Which of the following instruments is used to find out absorption of functional groups?
71820.sol:
Fourier transform Infrared (FTIR) spectrophotometer is used to identify functional groups in organic molecules. Different functional groups absorb characteristic frequencies of infrared radiation, which causes vibrational transitions in the bonds.

X-ray diffractometer is used to determine the crystal structure of a solid.

UV-visible spectrophotometer is used to study electronic transitions, typically in conjugated systems or transition metal complexes.

Scanning electron microscope is used to study the surface morphology and topography of a sample.

Therefore, FTIR is the correct instrument for finding the absorption of functional groups.

Answer: Fourier transform Infrared spectrophotometer

72310.subject: Physics
72310.text: Two radioactive materials A and B having decay constant '$7\lambda$' and '$\lambda$' respectively, initially have same number of nuclei. The time taken to have the ratio of number of nuclei of material B to that of A as '$e$', is
72310.sol:
Let the initial number of nuclei of both materials be $N_0$.

The number of nuclei of material A at time $t$ is given by $N_A = N_0 e^{-7\lambda t}$.

The number of nuclei of material B at time $t$ is given by $N_B = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$.

Given that the ratio of the number of nuclei of material B to that of A is $e$:

$\dfrac{N_B}{N_A} = e$

$\dfrac{N_0 e^{-\lambda t}}{N_0 e^{-7\lambda t}} = e$

$e^{6\lambda t} = e^1$

Equating the powers of $e$, we get:

$6\lambda t = 1$

$t = \dfrac{1}{6\lambda}$

Answer: $1/6\lambda$

72363.subject: Physics
72363.text: For an n-type semiconductor, the relation between the number density '$n_h$' and '$n_e$' is
72363.sol:
In an n-type semiconductor, pentavalent impurity atoms are added to the intrinsic semiconductor. Each impurity atom donates one free electron, significantly increasing the number density of electrons.

As a result, electrons become the majority charge carriers and holes become the minority charge carriers.

Therefore, the number density of electrons (n_e$) is much greater than the number density of holes (n_h$), which can be written as $n_h < < n_e$.

Answer: $n_h < < n_e$

Related Theory In light reaction of photosynthesis two types of photosystems are involved. PS-I consists of plenty of chlorophyll- $a$ and very less quantity of chlorophyll-b. It gets reduced after accepting electrons. It later gives this electron to ferredoxin and gets oxidized again.

81662.subject: Chemistry
81662.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
options: Carbon has the ability to form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bond with itself.
$\text{ECl}_3\ (E = B\ \text{and}\ \text{Al})$ is a monomer when $E = B$ and a dimer when $E = Al$.
The order of catenation property of Group 14 elements is $C >> Si > Ge \approx Sn$.
81662.sol:
Carbon has a strong tendency to form $p\pi$-$p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself, such as in alkenes and alkynes. Thus, the first statement is correct.

$\text{BCl}_3$ exists as a monomer because boron cannot expand its octet to form a dimer, whereas $\text{AlCl}_3$ exists as a dimer ($\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$) to complete its octet. Thus, the second statement is correct.

The catenation property depends on the element-element bond strength. The bond enthalpy decreases down the group, so the order of catenation is $C >> Si > Ge \approx Sn$. Thus, the third statement is correct.

Oxygen exhibits a $-2$ oxidation state in most of its compounds, but it also exhibits a $-1$ oxidation state in peroxides (e.g., $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$), a $-1/2$ oxidation state in superoxides (e.g., $\text{KO}_2$), and positive oxidation states when bonded to fluorine (e.g., $+2$ in $\text{OF}_2$ and $+1$ in $\text{O}_2\text{F}_2$). Thus, the fourth statement is incorrect.

Answer: Oxygen exhibits only $-2$ oxidation state.

81851.subject: Chemistry
81851.text: Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to :
options: increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component.
formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform.
stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules.
81851.sol:
Chloroform ($CHCl_3$) and acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$) form a non-ideal solution showing a negative deviation from Raoult's law.

This is because the hydrogen atom of chloroform forms a hydrogen bond with the oxygen atom of acetone.

The formation of this intermolecular hydrogen bond makes the attractive forces between the unlike molecules stronger than the attractive forces between the like molecules.

As a result, the escaping tendency of the molecules from the liquid phase decreases, leading to a lower vapour pressure than expected from Raoult's law.

Answer: formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform.

83603.subject: Physics
83603.text: A cup of coffee cools from $90 ° C$ to $80 ° C$ in $tmin$, when the room temperature is $20 ° C$. The time taken by a similar cup of coffee to cool from $80 ° C\text{to}60 ° C$ at a room temperature same at $20 ° C$ is :
83603.sol:
From Newton's Law of cooling,

$\dfrac{\DeltaT}{\Deltat} = k\left(T - {T}_{s}\right)$

where,

$⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{2} - {T}_{1}}{t} - k\left(\dfrac{{T}_{1} + {T}_{2}}{2} - {T}_{s}\right){T}_{s}$

Where, ${T}_{1} =$ Initial temperature of body

${T}_{2} =$ Final temperature of body

${T}_{s} =$ surrounding temperature

$t =$ time taken

For case$1,$

$\dfrac{90 - 80}{t} = k\left(\dfrac{90 + 80}{2} - 20\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{10}{t} = 65k$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{10}{65t} \ldots \left(i\right)$

For case $2,$

$\dfrac{80 - 60}{{t}^{'}} = k\left(\dfrac{80 + 60}{2} - 20\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{20}{{t}^{'}} = 50k$

Put the value $k$ from eq.$\left(\text{i}\right)$,

$⇒ \dfrac{20}{{t}^{'}} = 50 \times \dfrac{10}{65t}$

$⇒ {t}^{'} = \dfrac{20 \times 65}{500}t$

$⇒ {t}^{'} = \dfrac{13}{5}t$

91322.text: If $A$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix such that $A\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}- 1 \\ 2\end{array}\right]$ and $A^{2}\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$, then trace of $A$ is (where, the trace of the matrix is the sum of all principal diagonal elements of the matrix)

Let, $A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$
$A\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}- 1 \\ 2\end{array}\right] ⇒ \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}- 1 \\ 2\end{array}\right]$
On solving, we get,
$a - b = - 1, c - d = 2$
Also,
$A^{2}\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\right] = A\left(A\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ - 1\end{array}\right]\right) = A\left[\begin{array}{ll}- 1 \\ 2\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 0\end{array}\right]$
This gives, $- a + 2b = 1, - c + 2d = 0$
$⇒ b = 0, a = - 1, d = 2, c = 4$

Initially, the current was zero, so self-induced flux was also zero. Now when we rotate the loop, the change in flux is

$\Deltaϕ = 2\piR^{2} \times B$

Finally, to maintain the same zero flux, the current in the superconducting loop will be such that the flux due to induced current will negative of the flux due to external field

$L \times i = 2\piR^{2} \times B$.

$i = \dfrac{2\piR^{2} \times B}{L}$

93004.text: An equilateral triangular loop $ADC$ of uniform specific resistivity having some resistance is pulled with a constant velocity $v$ out of a uniform magnetic field directed into the paper. At time $t = 0$, side $DC$ of the loop is at the edge of the magnetic field. The induced current $\left(I\right)$ versus time $\left(t\right)$ graph will be as :
93004.sol:
Let $2a$ be the side of the triangle and $b$ the length $AE$.

$∆ AHG$ and $∆ AEC$ are similar triangles.

$\dfrac{AH}{AE} = \dfrac{GH}{EC}$

$∴ GH = \left(\dfrac{AH}{AE}\right)EC$

$= \dfrac{b - vt}{b} . a = a - \left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right)vt$

$∴ FG = 2GH = 2\left[a - \dfrac{a}{b}vt\right]$



Induced e.m.f., $e = Bv\left(FG\right) = 2Bv\left(a - \dfrac{a}{b}vt\right)$

$∴$ Induced current, $I = \dfrac{e}{R} = \dfrac{2Bv}{R}\left[a - \dfrac{a}{b}vt\right]$

or $I = {k}_{1} - {k}_{2}t$

Thus, the $I - t$ graph is a straight line with a negative slope and positive intercept.

The meiotic cell division comprises two successive nuclear division the meiosis I and meiosis II. The meiosis I have four stages prophase I, metaphase 1, anaphase 1, and telophase 1. The prophase I have further been divided into five phases depending on the chromosomal behavior.

The pachytene is the third phase of the five phases where the four chromatids appear as tetrads. Crossing over between two homologous chromosomes takes place during this phase and therefore leads to the recombination of the genetic material on the two chromosomes. In this phase the exchange of genetic material between sister chromatids of non- homologous chromosomes takes place. The& variations in sexually reproducing organisms are the result of this genetic recombination.

100524.subject: Physics
100524.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a coin is placed on a rotating record player, it is more likely to slip off if it is placed closer to the edge than near the center.
Reason (R): The required centripetal force for a particle moving in a circle of constant radius is directly proportional to the square of its angular velocity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
100524.sol:
For a coin placed on a rotating record player, the angular velocity $\omega$ is the same for all points.

The required centripetal force to prevent slipping is $F_c = m r \omega^2$. As the distance $r$ from the center increases (closer to the edge), the required centripetal force increases. Since the maximum static friction $f_s = \mu m g$ is constant, the coin is more likely to slip at a larger radius. Thus, the Assertion is true.

The Reason states that for a constant radius, $F_c \propto \omega^2$. This is a true statement based on $F_c = m r \omega^2$. However, it does not explain the Assertion, which is based on the variation of $F_c$ with radius $r$ at a constant $\omega$.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

100583.subject: Physics
100583.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: An elevator can go up or down with uniform speed when its weight is balanced with the tension of its cable.
Statement-II: Force exerted by the floor of an elevator on the foot of a person standing on it is more than his/her weight when the elevator goes down with increasing speed.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
100583.sol:
When elevator is moving with uniform speed $T = {F}_{g}$, as the net force along the vertical direction should be zero.

Therefore, Statement-I is true.

Now, when elevator is going down with increasing speed, its acceleration is downward.
Hence, 

$W - N = ma$
$⇒ W - N = \dfrac{W}{g} \times a$

$⇒ N = W\left(1 - \dfrac{a}{g}\right)$

Clearly, normal reaction is less than weight. So Statement-II is false.

102643.subject: Physics
102643.text: A closed organ pipe and an open organ pipe have the same physical length of $30\text{ cm}$ and the same radius of $5\text{ cm}$. Taking the end correction into account, what is the ratio of the fundamental frequency of the closed pipe to that of the open pipe? (Assume the end correction $e = 0.6r$, where $r$ is the radius of the pipe)
102643.sol:
For a closed organ pipe, the end correction is applied at one end.
Effective length of the closed pipe, $L_{c} = L + 0.6r$
$L_{c} = 30 + 0.6(5) = 33\text{ cm}$

For an open organ pipe, the end correction is applied at both ends.
Effective length of the open pipe, $L_{o} = L + 2(0.6r) = L + 1.2r$
$L_{o} = 30 + 1.2(5) = 36\text{ cm}$

The fundamental frequency of a closed pipe is given by $f_{c} = \dfrac{v}{4L_{c}}$
$f_{c} = \dfrac{v}{4 \times 33} = \dfrac{v}{132}$

The fundamental frequency of an open pipe is given by $f_{o} = \dfrac{v}{2L_{o}}$
$f_{o} = \dfrac{v}{2 \times 36} = \dfrac{v}{72}$

The ratio of their fundamental frequencies is:
$\dfrac{f_{c}}{f_{o}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{v}{132}}{\dfrac{v}{72}} = \dfrac{72}{132} = \dfrac{6}{11}$

Answer: $6 : 11$

102648.subject: Physics
102648.text: A progressive wave is represented by the equation $y = A \sin(\alpha x - \beta t)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres and $t$ is in seconds. If the frequency of the wave is $n$ and its propagation speed is $v$, then the parameter $\alpha$ is given by:
102648.sol:
The standard equation of a travelling wave is $y = A \sin(kx - \omega t)$.

Comparing this with the given equation $y = A \sin(\alpha x - \beta t)$, we identify the parameter $\alpha$ as the wave number $k$.

The wave number is related to the wavelength $\lambda$ by the formula $k = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}$.

The relationship between wave speed $v$, frequency $n$, and wavelength $\lambda$ is $v = n\lambda$, which rearranges to $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{n}$.

Substituting this expression for $\lambda$ into the equation for $\alpha$, we get:
$\alpha = \dfrac{2\pi}{\left(\dfrac{v}{n}\right)} = \dfrac{2\pi n}{v}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{2\pi n}{v}$

103301.subject: Physics
103301.text: Two heating coils, one rated $100$ W, $220$ V and the other rated $300$ W, $220$ V, are connected in series across a $220$ V supply. What is the total power consumed by the series combination?
103301.sol:
The resistance of a heating coil is given by $R = \dfrac{V^2}{P}$.

For the first coil: $R_1 = \dfrac{220^2}{100} \, \Omega$
For the second coil: $R_2 = \dfrac{220^2}{300} \, \Omega$

When connected in series, the equivalent resistance is $R_{\text{eq}} = R_1 + R_2$.

$R_{\text{eq}} = \dfrac{220^2}{100} + \dfrac{220^2}{300} = 220^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{100} + \dfrac{1}{300} \right) = 220^2 \left( \dfrac{3 + 1}{300} \right) = 220^2 \left( \dfrac{4}{300} \right) \, \Omega$

The total power consumed by the series combination across the $220$ V supply is:
$P_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{V^2}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \dfrac{220^2}{220^2 \left( \dfrac{4}{300} \right)} = \dfrac{300}{4} = 75$ W.

Alternatively, for two appliances in series across their rated voltage, the equivalent power can be found directly using $P_{\text{eq}} = \dfrac{P_1 P_2}{P_1 + P_2} = \dfrac{100 \times 300}{100 + 300} = \dfrac{30000}{400} = 75$ W.

Answer: $75$ W

103660.subject: Physics
103660.text: A uniform electric field and a uniform magnetic field are acting along the positive x-axis in a certain region. A proton is projected into this region with its initial velocity directed along the negative x-axis. Which of the following best describes the subsequent motion of the proton?
options: It will move in a circular path.
Its speed will increase and it will move in a straight line.
Its speed will decrease and it will move in a straight line.
It will move in a helical path.
103660.sol:
The magnetic force on the proton is $\vec{F}_m = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$. Since the velocity is anti-parallel to the magnetic field ($\theta = 180^\circ$), the magnetic force is zero. Thus, the magnetic field does not change the path of the proton.

The electric force on the positively charged proton is $\vec{F}_e = q\vec{E}$, which acts in the direction of the electric field (positive x-axis). Since the proton is moving along the negative x-axis, the electric force acts opposite to its direction of motion.

Therefore, the proton experiences a retarding force, causing it to decelerate while continuing to move in a straight line. Its speed will decrease.

Answer: Its speed will decrease and it will move in a straight line.

104474.subject: Physics
104474.text:
A ray of light is incident normally on one face of an equilateral glass prism. Consider the following statements regarding the path of the ray:

I. The angle of incidence at the second face is $60^{\circ}$.
II. For the ray to emerge from the second face, the refractive index of the prism must be less than or equal to $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$.
III. If the refractive index of the prism is $1.5$, the ray undergoes total internal reflection at the second face.
IV. If the refractive index of the prism is $\sqrt{2}$, the ray emerges grazing the second face.

Choose the correct combination of valid statements:
104474.sol:
Since the ray is incident normally on the first face, $i_1 = 0^{\circ}$, which means the angle of refraction at the first face $r_1 = 0^{\circ}$.

For a prism, $r_1 + r_2 = A$. For an equilateral prism, $A = 60^{\circ}$. Thus, the angle of incidence at the second face $r_2 = 60^{\circ} - 0^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$. (Statement I is correct)

For the ray to emerge, $r_2 \le C$, where $C$ is the critical angle.
$\sin(60^{\circ}) \le \sin C = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$
$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \le \dfrac{1}{\mu} \Rightarrow \mu \le \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 1.15$. (Statement II is correct)

If $\mu = 1.5$, it is greater than $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$. Hence, the angle of incidence ($60^{\circ}$) is greater than the critical angle, and the ray undergoes total internal reflection. (Statement III is correct)

If $\mu = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$, it is also greater than $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$, so the ray will undergo total internal reflection. It will not emerge grazing the second face (which only happens if $\mu = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$). (Statement IV is incorrect)

Answer: I, II and III only

104692.subject: Physics
104692.text: Unpolarized light of intensity $I_0$ passes through four polaroids arranged in series. The transmission axis of each subsequent polaroid is rotated by an angle of $30^{\circ}$ relative to the preceding one. What is the final transmitted intensity of light through the fourth polaroid?
104692.sol:
When unpolarized light of intensity $I_0$ passes through the first polaroid, its intensity is halved:
$I_1 = \dfrac{I_0}{2}$

The light then passes through the second polaroid, whose axis is at $30^{\circ}$ to the first. According to Malus's Law:
$I_2 = I_1 \cos^2(30^{\circ}) = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{4}$

The third polaroid is at $30^{\circ}$ to the second:
$I_3 = I_2 \cos^2(30^{\circ}) = \left(\dfrac{I_0}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{4}\right) \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^2$

The fourth polaroid is at $30^{\circ}$ to the third:
$I_4 = I_3 \cos^2(30^{\circ}) = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^2 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^3$

Calculating the final value:
$I_4 = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \times \dfrac{27}{64} = \dfrac{27 I_0}{128}$

Answer: $\dfrac{27 I_0}{128}$

104998.subject: Physics
104998.text: A nuclear reactor generates power at a steady rate of $1000 \text{ MW}$. What is the mass converted into energy during $1 \text{ hour}$ of its operation, in milligrams?
104998.sol:
The total energy produced by the reactor in $1 \text{ hour}$ is calculated using the relation between energy, power, and time:
$E = P \times t$

Given $P = 1000 \text{ MW} = 10^9 \text{ W}$ and $t = 1 \text{ hour} = 3600 \text{ s}$:
$E = 10^9 \times 3600 = 3.6 \times 10^{12} \text{ J}$

According to the mass-energy equivalence principle, $E = mc^2$.
The mass $m$ converted into energy is:
$m = \dfrac{E}{c^2}$
$m = \dfrac{3.6 \times 10^{12}}{(3 \times 10^8)^2}$
$m = \dfrac{3.6 \times 10^{12}}{9 \times 10^{16}}$
$m = 0.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ kg} = 4 \times 10^{-5} \text{ kg}$

To convert this mass into milligrams:
$1 \text{ kg} = 10^3 \text{ g} = 10^6 \text{ mg}$
$m = 4 \times 10^{-5} \times 10^6 \text{ mg} = 40 \text{ mg}$

Answer: $40$
104998.meta: A nuclear reactor generates power at a steady rate of 1000 MW . What is the mass converted into energy during 1 hour of its operation, in milligrams?

105231.subject: Physics
105231.text: In a logic circuit, input $A$ is connected to both inputs of a NOR gate to produce an output $Y_1$. Similarly, input $B$ is connected to both inputs of a second NOR gate to produce an output $Y_2$. The outputs $Y_1$ and $Y_2$ are then fed as the two inputs to a third NOR gate, which produces the final output $Y$. The simplified Boolean expression for the final output $Y$ is:
105231.sol:
A NOR gate with both inputs tied together acts as a NOT gate.

For the first NOR gate, the inputs are $A$ and $A$. Its output is $Y_1 = \overline{A + A} = \bar{A}$.

For the second NOR gate, the inputs are $B$ and $B$. Its output is $Y_2 = \overline{B + B} = \bar{B}$.

These outputs are fed into the third NOR gate. The final output is $Y = \overline{Y_1 + Y_2} = \overline{\bar{A} + \bar{B}}$.

Applying De Morgan's theorem ($\overline{X + Y} = \bar{X} \cdot \bar{Y}$), we get:
$Y = \overline{\overline{A}} \cdot \overline{\overline{B}} = A \cdot B$.

Answer: $A \cdot B$

105423.subject: Physics
105423.text: In a certain vernier callipers, $10$ divisions of the vernier scale coincide with $8$ divisions of the main scale. The length of one main scale division is $1$ mm. When measuring the diameter of a sphere, the zero of the vernier scale lies just after the $3.2$ cm mark on the main scale, and the $4^{\text{th}}$ division of the vernier scale exactly coincides with a main scale division. The measured diameter of the sphere is:
105423.sol:
First, we determine the least count (LC) of the vernier callipers.

Given $10$ VSD $= 8$ MSD, we have:

$1$ VSD $= \dfrac{8}{10}$ MSD $= 0.8$ MSD

Since $1$ MSD $= 1$ mm, $1$ VSD $= 0.8$ mm.

The least count is:

LC $= 1$ MSD $- 1$ VSD $= 1$ mm $- 0.8$ mm $= 0.2$ mm

Converting the least count to cm:

LC $= 0.02$ cm

Now, we calculate the total reading for the diameter of the sphere.

Main Scale Reading (MSR) $= 3.2$ cm

Vernier Scale Reading (VSR) $= 4$

Total Reading $= \text{MSR} + (\text{VSR} \times \text{LC})$

Total Reading $= 3.2 \text{ cm} + (4 \times 0.02 \text{ cm}) = 3.2 \text{ cm} + 0.08 \text{ cm} = 3.28 \text{ cm}$

Answer: $3.28$ cm

106427.subject: Chemistry
106427.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a multi-electron atom, an electron will occupy the $3d$ orbital before the $4p$ orbital.
Reason (R): The $(n+l)$ value for the $3d$ orbital is lower than the $(n+l)$ value for the $4p$ orbital.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
106427.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: According to the Aufbau principle, electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy. The $3d$ orbital has lower energy than the $4p$ orbital, so it is occupied first.

Reason (R) is false: The energy of an orbital is determined by the $(n+l)$ rule. For the $3d$ orbital, $n=3$ and $l=2$, giving $(n+l) = 5$. For the $4p$ orbital, $n=4$ and $l=1$, also giving $(n+l) = 5$. The values are equal, not lower.

When two orbitals have the same $(n+l)$ value, the orbital with the lower value of $n$ has lower energy and is filled first. This is why $3d$ ($n=3$) is filled before $4p$ ($n=4$).

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

107744.subject: Chemistry
107744.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The molecule $\text{Ne}_2$ does not exist.
Reason (R): In the molecular orbital diagram of $\text{Ne}_2$, the number of antibonding electrons is greater than the number of bonding electrons.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
107744.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct because the $\text{Ne}_2$ molecule has a bond order of zero, indicating that no chemical bond is formed and the molecule does not exist.

Reason (R) is incorrect. A neon atom has 10 electrons, so the hypothetical $\text{Ne}_2$ molecule would have 20 electrons. Its molecular orbital configuration is $\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^{*} 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^{*} 2s^2 \sigma 2p_z^2 (\pi 2p_x^2 = \pi 2p_y^2) (\pi^{*} 2p_x^2 = \pi^{*} 2p_y^2) \sigma^{*} 2p_z^2$.

The number of bonding electrons ($N_b$) is 10 and the number of antibonding electrons ($N_a$) is 10. Since $N_b = N_a$, the bond order is $\dfrac{1}{2}[10 - 10] = 0$. The number of antibonding electrons is equal to, not greater than, the number of bonding electrons.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

107800.subject: Chemistry
107800.text: Which of the following pairs of species are isostructural?
107800.sol:
Isostructural species have the same molecular shape.

For $\text{NH}_3$: Central N has 5 valence electrons. It forms 3 bonds and has 1 lone pair. Shape: Trigonal pyramidal.
For $\text{BF}_3$: Central B has 3 valence electrons. It forms 3 bonds and has 0 lone pairs. Shape: Trigonal planar.

For $\text{SF}_4$: Central S has 6 valence electrons. It forms 4 bonds and has 1 lone pair. Shape: See-saw.
For $\text{CH}_4$: Central C has 4 valence electrons. It forms 4 bonds and has 0 lone pairs. Shape: Tetrahedral.

For $\text{BCl}_3$: Central B has 3 valence electrons. It forms 3 bonds and has 0 lone pairs. Shape: Trigonal planar.
For $\text{PCl}_3$: Central P has 5 valence electrons. It forms 3 bonds and has 1 lone pair. Shape: Trigonal pyramidal.

For $\text{XeF}_2$: Central Xe has 8 valence electrons. It forms 2 bonds and has 3 lone pairs. The lone pairs occupy equatorial positions of a trigonal bipyramid. Shape: Linear.
For $\text{I}_3^-$: Central I has 7 valence electrons + 1 anionic charge = 8 electrons. It forms 2 bonds with the other I atoms and has 3 lone pairs. Shape: Linear.

Thus, $\text{XeF}_2$ and $\text{I}_3^-$ are isostructural.

Answer: $\text{XeF}_2$ and $\text{I}_3^-$

123637.subject: Botany
123637.text: In some organisms, what happens if karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis?
options: A multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium
A single nuclei condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium
A multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of multiple nuclei
A single nuclei condition arises leading to the formation of multiple nuclei
123637.sol: Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, thererfore they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. At the time of cytoplasmic division, organelles like mitochondria and plastids get distributed between the two daughter cells. In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis as a result of which multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).

Electron micrographs of this stage indicate that chromosome synapsis is accompanied by the formation of complex structure called synaptonemal complex. The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad. However, these are more clearly visible at the next stage. The first two stages of prophase I are relatively short-lived compared to the next stage that is pachytene.

126470.subject: Botany
126470.text: What is the result of straining the slurry through a cheesecloth or cotton?
126470.sol: We can take any living tissue (a vegetable or a piece of liver, etc.) and grind it in trichloroacetic acid (Cl3CCOOH) using a mortar and a pestle. We obtain a thick slurry. Ifwe were to strain this through a cheesecloth or cotton we would obtain two fractions. One is called the filtrate or more technically, the acid-soluble pool, and the second, the retentate or the acid-insoluble fraction. Scientists have found thousands of organic compounds in the acid-soluble pool.

127212.subject: Botany
127212.text: How many medicinally useful plants are believed to be in tropical rainforests?
127212.sol: The narrowly utilitarian arguments for conserving biodiversity are obvious; humans derive countless direct economic benefits from naturefood (cereals, pulses, fruits), firewood, fibre, construction material, industrial products (tannins, lubricants, dyes, resins, perfumes ) and products of medicinal importance. More than 25 per cent of the drugs currently sold in the market worldwide are derived from plants and 25,000 species of plants contribute to the traditional medicines used by native peoples around the world. Nobody knows how many more medicinally useful plants there are in tropical rain forests waiting to be explored. With increasing resources put into ‘bioprospecting’ (exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance), nations endowed with rich biodiversity can expect to reap enormous benefits

127770.subject: Botany
127770.text: In a grazing food chain consisting of Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Frog $\rightarrow$ Snake, the energy available at the producer level is $5,00,000 \text{ J}$. What amount of energy will be available to the secondary consumer in this food chain?
127770.sol:
The given food chain is: Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Frog $\rightarrow$ Snake.

Here, Grass is the producer (first trophic level, $T_1$).
Grasshopper is the primary consumer (second trophic level, $T_2$).
Frog is the secondary consumer (third trophic level, $T_3$).

Energy at the producer level ($T_1$) = $5,00,000 \text{ J}$.

According to Lindeman's 10% law, only 10% of the energy is transferred to the next trophic level.
Energy available to the primary consumer (Grasshopper) = 10% of $5,00,000 \text{ J} = 50,000 \text{ J}$.
Energy available to the secondary consumer (Frog) = 10% of $50,000 \text{ J} = 5,000 \text{ J}$.

Therefore, the energy available to the secondary consumer is $5,000 \text{ J}$.

Answer: $5,000 \text{ J}$

127811.subject: Botany
127811.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The pyramid of biomass in a sea is generally inverted.
Reason (R): The biomass of fishes far exceeds that of phytoplankton.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
127811.sol:
Assertion is true. In aquatic ecosystems such as a sea or pond, the pyramid of biomass is generally inverted.

Reason is also true and correctly explains the Assertion. The pyramid is inverted because the standing crop of phytoplankton (producers) is much lower than the standing crop of fishes (consumers) that depend on them. Phytoplankton have a very high turnover rate (rapid reproduction and short lifespan), allowing a small biomass to support a much larger biomass of fishes.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
